- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) within 3–5 days, model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 1–3% to next 5–7 day horizon.
- After a strong upward spike in price, model frequently overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above recent peak.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0–0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for latent bullish bias.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends when sentiment is weak; if sentiment drops below 0.0 for 3+ consecutive days, apply a 1–2% downward adjustment to next 7-day forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent volatility; use 10–15 day moving average as baseline for smoothing out short-term noise.
